summary: Decompose god function execute patch transaction

delivery.outcome: Decompose execute_patch_transaction in src/koru/queue/transaction/service.py: extract the pre-plan screens into _screen_before_plan returning a _ScreenedPatch NamedTuple (star-unpacked so the tuple double-count quirk stays out), and the journal open, invalid-verify refusal, artifact delivery, promotion gates and isolated/direct dispatch into _open_run_journal, _refuse_invalid_verify_profile, _deliver_artifact, _screen_promotion_gates and _run_plan, dropping the function from CC=10 / fan-out=14 / mutations=21 to CC=6 / fan-out=9 / mutations=6 (god-function thresholds: fan-out > 10, mutations > 6, CC > 12) while preserving the journal event sequence, refusal codes and messages, and the public execute_patch_transaction contract.
nonGoals: Reducing the pre-existing mutations of _run_isolated and _apply_to_workspace (12 each, unchanged by this ticket)
Changing extract_patch's plain-tuple return contract in preflight.py (outside this ticket's allowed paths)

architecture.decision: Extract one helper per phase of the orchestrator and star-unpack extract_patch's tuple into a _ScreenedPatch NamedTuple, which keeps the orchestrator free of tuple-unpack targets (code2llm double-counts them as mutations) and of journal.append calls (the append method-name heuristic also counts as a mutation).
architecture.rollback: Revert the commit to restore the inline phase blocks in execute_patch_transaction.

commands: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; from code2llm import ProjectAnalyzer, Config; r = ProjectAnalyzer(Config(), Path('<probe-dir>')).analyze_project(Path('<probe-dir>')); import sys; muts = {}; [muts.__setitem__(m.scope, muts.get(m.scope, 0) + 1) for m in r.mutations]; print({n: (i.complexity.get('cyclomatic_complexity', 1), r.metrics.get(n, {}).get('fan_out', 0), muts.get(n, 0)) for n, i in r.functions.items()})"
validation.evidence: execute_patch_transaction measures CC=6, fan-out=9, mutations=6, and every helper introduced by this ticket measures under all three god-function thresholds.
All existing phase tests pass unchanged and the new TestOrchestratorJournal tests pin the resolved/frozen/completed and resolved/refused event sequences.
